paper_metadata.title: PO-QA: A Framework for Portfolio Optimization using Quantum Algorithms

summary: The paper studies portfolio optimization on 8 stocks over a 6-month period using two gate-based algorithms, QAOA and VQE, each evaluated across 12 circuit architectures (B-M) and 9 risk values from 0.1 to 0.9. The main quantitative finding is that QAOA is more stable and matches the exact eigensolver classical benchmark more often than VQE, while VQE shows strong sensitivity to circuit design and risk, especially around risk = 0.5.

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization evaluated with QAOA across 12 circuit architectures (B–M) and risk factors 0.1–0.9, compared against an exact classical eigensolver benchmark.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio optimization is converted via quadratic programming to a ground-state energy minimization problem; the paper does not specify the exact qubit-to-variable mapping.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the ground-state energy corresponding to the portfolio optimization Hamiltonian; compare quantum solution energy to exact eigensolver benchmark.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Quadratic programming with linear constraints; penalty formulation details not specified.

problem_instance.description: Real-market portfolio optimization on 8 stocks over a 6-month period.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Historical financial data converted to quadratic program using mean returns and covariance; budget set to assets/2; risk factor swept from 0.1 to 0.9

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use historical mean returns (mu) and covariance (sigma) from the 6-month price series; formulate the portfolio optimization as a quadratic program with linear constraints.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: For each of 12 circuit configurations and 9 risk values, compare the predicted ground-state energy and whether the solution matches the exact eigensolver benchmark.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical market data collection and quadratic-program formulation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare quantum and classical ground-state energies; compute match/non-match to classical benchmark and similarity percentages.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Ground-state energy convergence/variability across circuit configurations and risk values

speedup_claims.conditions: Comparison is qualitative/benchmark-based only; no runtime or asymptotic speedup reported.
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports better convergence/matching for QAOA in many cases, but does not claim or demonstrate computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not enough hardware/resource data reported; only algorithmic comparison on 8-asset portfolio instances with 9 risk settings and 12 circuit variants.
limiting_factors: No runtime, shot count, or noise model reported
Comparison is against an exact eigensolver classical benchmark
No demonstrated quantum advantage; QAOA is reported as mostly matching or outperforming VQE, not classical

notes: Hardware type is not explicitly named; inferred as not_specified because the paper only states Qiskit-based experiments and does not name a real QPU or simulator backend.
Num qubits is not explicitly stated; the paper gives 8 assets, but the exact qubit register size/mapping is not reported, so it remains inferred/not specified rather than guessed.
The paper reports comparison to an exact eigensolver but does not provide asymptotic complexity or a proven speedup claim.
The paper reports QAOA results for 12 circuit architectures (B-M) over 9 risk values (0.1-0.9) on an 8-asset portfolio, but does not provide evidence of advantage over classical computing.
